decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents saving flow; client reveals its content: 'The spec makes the title something I must enter and explicitly leaves automatic fetching out.' Client responds correctively: 'I don't want to have to type the title myself every time ... I paste a web address and the app fills in the page's title (and ideally its description/icon) automatically ... I'd like saving a bookmark from just the address, with the title pulled in for me, to be part of this first release ... still be able to edit that title afterward.' Round 2 maker adopts it (auto title/description/icon, fallback, editable).
decisions.note: Specification gate. Divergence established from client's description of the presented spec (mandatory title, auto-fetch explicitly excluded), contradicting REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon) and URL-only save REF-BM-01, with REF-BM-03 editable retained. Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour in place of the mismatch.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: '... page archiving are outside the initial release.' Client explicitly identifies and accepts: 'I'm fine leaving sharing, imports, extensions, and page archiving for later.' Re-expressed at round 5 postscript: 'For somewhere down the road, not now: ... to save whole pages for offline reading. No changes needed today.'
decisions.note: Specification gate (reinforced at implementation review). Reference includes local HTML snapshot (REF-BM-24) and Internet Archive snapshot (REF-BM-25); presentation omits them (divergence from reference ceiling). Client names the feature and accepts the departure without requesting alignment. Round-5 restatement logged but not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: '... imports ... are outside the initial release.' Client: 'I'm fine leaving sharing, imports, extensions ... for later.' Re-expressed round 5: 'it'd be nice to bring in my existing bookmarks from a file ... No changes needed today.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. REF-BM-30 (Netscape HTML import) omitted from presented scope = divergence from reference. Client explicitly identifies the deferred feature and accepts the departure. Round-5 restatement recorded, not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Across all presentations the maker lists 'favorites' but never a read-later/unread state or an unread view: round 1 '... tags, favorites, search, filters ...'; round 5 delivered set '... tags, favorites, search, filters, pagination, editing, archiving/restoring, and confirmed deletion.' Client repeatedly endorses 'favorites' (rounds 1,3,4,5) and never raises read-later; no mark-as-read or unread-only view is mentioned anywhere.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference requires a read-later/unread flag (REF-BM-17), a separate unread-only view (REF-BM-18), and mark-as-read to clear it (REF-BM-19); the presented feature set substitutes non-reference 'favorites' (starring), which is not functionally equivalent. The difference passes without corrective response or explicit expression by the client. diverged=true is inferred from the consistent presence of favorites and absence of any read-state feature across presentations.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker delivers 'archiving/restoring, and confirmed deletion'; round 1 client: 'archiving, and delete-with-confirmation all look right'; round 5 client: 'edit, archive, restore, or delete with a confirmation.'
decisions.note: Recorded in-scope decision conforming to reference: reversible archive/restore (REF-BM-26/28) distinct from permanent delete (REF-BM-27, REF-BM-05). Client engaged with and endorsed it; no divergence to capture.
